sections.title: SRN OH VALLEY/TN VALLEY
sections.text: A FAST-MOVING UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH OVER THE SRN PLAINS WILL MOVE EWD INTO THE MID-MS VALLEY TODAY. A BROAD MOIST SECTOR WILL BE IN PLACE AHEAD OF THE SYSTEM FROM THE CNTRL GULF COAST STATES NNEWD INTO THE OH VALLEY. ON THE NWRN EDGE OF THE WARM SECTOR...A LARGE MCS WILL LIKELY BE ONGOING AT 12Z FROM NEAR THE OH RIVER SWD ACROSS KY INTO NRN AND WRN TN. FORECAST SOUNDINGS ALONG AND SOUTH OF THIS CORRIDOR MONDAY MORNING SHOW VERY FAVORABLE WIND SHEAR PROFILES FOR SEVERE STORMS. A LINE SEGMENT WITH NUMEROUS SEVERE STORMS SHOULD GRADUALLY MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE MODERATE RISK AREA DURING THE DAY. ON THE WRN EDGE OF THE LOW-LEVEL JET...FORECAST SOUNDINGS ESTIMATE 0-3 KM STORM RELATIVE HELICITIES TO BE IN THE 400 TO 500 M2/S2 RANGE ACROSS A LARGE AREA MAKING CONDITIONS FAVORABLE FOR TORNADOES. SEVERAL STRONG TORNADOES SHOULD OCCUR WITH THE MORE INTENSE ROTATING CELLS EMBEDDED WITHIN THE LINE. A WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD ALSO EXIST ACROSS A LARGE AREA. VERY STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE BETTER ORGANIZED BOWING LINE-SEGMENTS. THE SQUALL-LINE SHOULD MOVE SEWD INTO CNTRL AL AND NRN GA DURING THE LATE AFTERNOON WHERE A SEVERE THREAT SHOULD PERSIST DUE TO THE FAVORABLE WIND SHEAR ENVIR

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY/MID-ATLANTIC/CAROLINAS
sections.text: A BROAD LOW-LEVEL JET WILL BE IN PLACE ACROSS THE SRN APPALACHIAN MTNS THIS MORNING. THUNDERSTORMS SHOULD BE ONGOING AT 12Z ON THE WRN EDGE OF THE LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS SRN OH WITH THIS CONVECTION EXPANDING EWD ACROSS WV AND SRN PA THIS AFTERNOON. ALTHOUGH A TORNADO THREAT MAY DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF THE CNTRL APPALACHIAN MTNS DUE TO THE VERY STRONG LOW-LEVEL SHEAR...THE GREATEST TORNADO THREAT SHOULD EXIST SWWD ACROSS ERN KY WHERE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL BE MORE FAVORABLE AND SFC DEWPOINTS COULD REACH 60 F. FURTHER TO THE NORTHEAST IN WV...WRN VA AND MD...THE MAIN THREAT SHOULD BE WIND DAMAGE AS A LINE MOVES OVER THE CREST OF THE APPALACHIAN MTNS THIS AFTERNOON. AS THE LINE MOVES EWD INTO THE MID-ATLANTIC AND COASTAL PLAINS OF THE CAROLINAS...A WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD DEVELOP THIS EVENING. ..BROYLES.. 02/28/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: POTENT SHORT-WAVE TROUGH CURRENTLY FROM THE OZARK PLATEAU TO RED RIVER VALLEY WILL TRANSLATE RAPIDLY EWD...MOVING OFF THE ATLANTIC COAST LATE TONIGHT INTO TUE MORNING. THIS SYSTEM WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A 80-100 KT MIDLEVEL JET STREAK AND A CORRIDOR OF HEIGHT FALLS EXCEEDING 50-100 M/12-HR. AT THE SURFACE...LEAD LOW PRESSURE CENTER OVER THE LOWER GREAT LAKES WILL DEVELOP NEWD THROUGH NRN NEW ENGLAND/ST. LAWRENCE VALLEY TODAY WITH TRAILING COLD FRONT PUSHING EWD/SEWD THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE OH VALLEY AND MID ATLANTIC STATES. THE SWRN EXTENSION OF THIS FRONT LINKS WITH A SECONDARY LOW PRESSURE CENTER CURRENTLY NEAR THE CONFLUENCE OF THE MS AND OH RIVERS...AND THIS LOW IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP NEWD ALONG COLD FRONT TO VICINITY OF THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS BY AFTERNOON. MEANWHILE...SEGMENT OF COLD FRONT TRAILING FROM THE SECONDARY LOW PRESSURE WILL STEADILY MOVE E/SE THROUGH THE TN VALLEY AND GULF COAST STATES.

sections.title: LOWER MS/OH VALLEYS EWD TO THE ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: AN EXPANSIVE PRE-FRONTAL QLCS IS ONGOING AS OF 12Z FROM THE UPPER OH VALLEY SWWD TO INTO CNTRL KY. FARTHER S...A MORE RECENT INTENSIFICATION OF STORMS HAS BEEN OBSERVED IN THE WAKE OF A GRAVITY WAVE OVER THE LOWER MS VALLEY. LATEST MESOSCALE AND CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGEST THAT ONGOING QLCS WILL CONTINUE EWD THROUGH THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES TODAY ALONG AND S OF WARM FRONT RETREATING NWD THROUGH THE REGION. 12Z OBSERVED AND MODEL FORECAST SOUNDINGS INDICATE VERY STRONG WIND FIELDS WHICH WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF EMBEDDED BOWS AND SUPERCELLS WITH A RISK FOR CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE AND A FEW TORNADOES. OVER THE TN VALLEY INTO GULF COAST STATES....EXPECT STORMS TO INCREASE IN BOTH COVERAGE AND INTENSITY TODAY AS HEIGHT FALLS ASSOCIATED WITH MIDLEVEL TROUGH PROGRESSIVELY OVERSPREAD THE WARM SECTOR. BASED ON CURRENT RADAR TRENDS...AND TO SOME EXTENT SIMULATED REFLECTIVITY FORECASTS FROM A COUPLE HIGH-RESOLUTION MODELS...THERE WILL BE A GREATER POTENTIAL FOR DISCRETE STORMS INTERSPERSED WITH SMALLER-SCALE BOWING SYSTEMS. GIVEN THE COMPARATIVELY STRONGER BUOYANCY THAN POINTS N AND EQUALLY STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR /REFERENCE 12Z BNA SOUNDING/...IT APPEARS

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN EXTENSIVE SQUALL LINE IS ONGOING FROM ERN KY NEWD TO NRN VA/MD...IN ADVANCE OF A SURFACE COLD FRONT. IN THE WAKE OF AN INITIAL CYCLONE NEAR LAKE ONTARIO...THIS COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE APPALACHIANS TODAY...AND OFF THE MID ATLANTIC AND CAROLINA COASTS BY EARLY TONIGHT. A SECONDARY WAVE ON THE FRONT IN NE AR THIS MORNING WILL PROGRESS EWD ACROSS TN TODAY TO NC BY THIS EVENING...IN ADVANCE OF THE PRIMARY MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH NOW OVER MO/AR.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC REGION THROUGH THIS EVENING
sections.text: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY AND SURFACE OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST THAT SUBSTANTIAL SURFACE HEATING WILL OCCUR E OF THE APPALACHIANS TODAY IN ADVANCE OF THE PRE-FRONTAL SQUALL LINE. THIS HEATING...COMBINED WITH BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS OF 55-60 F...WILL SUPPORT STEEPENING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND SUFFICIENT SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY TO RESULT IN REJUVENATION OF THE SQUALL LINE E OF THE MOUNTAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. AT THE SAME TIME...DEEP-LAYER WINDS WILL INCREASE WITH THE APPROACH OF THE MIDLEVEL WAVE...AND VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN STRONG. THE ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT THE MAINTENANCE OF A PRIMARILY LINEAR CONVECTIVE SYSTEM FROM NC NWD INTO THE MID ATLANTIC...WHERE DAMAGING WINDS AND A COUPLE OF QLCS TORNADOES WILL BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREATS.

sections.title: SE STATES THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: THE SCENARIO IS A LITTLE MORE COMPLEX INVOF THE SRN APPALACHIANS /AL AND TN TO THE PIEDMONT/. THE CONVECTION IS ORIENTED MORE E-W ACROSS TN ON THE TRAILING END OF THE APPALACHIANS SQUALL LINE...WITH OTHER NNE-SSW BROKEN BANDS OF CONVECTION EXTENDING SWD INTO THE WARM SECTOR ACROSS NE MS AND MIDDLE TN. THE RICHEST MOISTURE FEED EXTENDS FROM MS/AL NEWD INTO SE TN AND NW GA. REGIONAL 12Z SOUNDINGS FROM OHX AND BMX REVEALED AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF TORNADIC SUPERCELLS...AND THE 16Z JAN SOUNDING SHOWED SOME WEAKENING OF CONVECTIVE INHIBITION NEAR 800 MB SINCE 12Z. INTENSIFICATION AND SWD EXPANSION OF THE CONVECTIVE BAND IN MS WILL OCCUR BY EARLY AFTERNOON IN AL...IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE REMNANT DRYLINE/LEE TROUGH AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER WARMS AND THE CAP WEAKENS. A BROKEN LINE WITH EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY CONVECTIVE MODE...WITH AN ATTENDANT RISK FOR A FEW TORNADOES...LARGE HAIL...AND DAMAGING WINDS THROUGH THIS EVENING. THE CONVECTIVE LINE IS EXPECTED TO WEAKEN OVERNIGHT WHILE APPROACHING THE SE ATLANTIC COAST ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 02/28/2011
